# sws-seven-segment-lcd

A reusable seven-segment readout for MSFS 2024 HTML/TypeScript instruments. It draws the digits as SVG inside an element you provide, and rewrites only the segments that changed, so it is cheap to update every frame.

## Developer guide

The full guide, with figures and the complete API reference, is [docs/SevenSegment_Developer_Guide.pdf](docs/SevenSegment_Developer_Guide.pdf). This page is the short version.

## Requirements

- Access to this private repository. Ask the owner to add your GitHub account as a collaborator.
- Node.js (with npm) and Git.

## Install

Run this in your instrument project's folder:

```powershell
npm install git+https://github.com/EvripidesEfthymiou/sws-seven-segment-lcd.git
```

The first time, Git may ask you to sign in to GitHub.

To move to a newer version later, run the same command again and rebuild your project.

## Use

Add an empty element to the instrument's HTML:

```html
<div id="busVolts"></div>
```

Create the readout and give it a value:

```ts
import { SevenSegmentReadout } from 'sws-seven-segment-lcd';

const busVolts = new SevenSegmentReadout(document.getElementById('busVolts')!, {
  digits: 3,
  decimals: 1,
  style: 'sws_dash8_bold_italic',
  digitHeight: 250,
  color: 'rgba(255, 216, 16, 0.72)',
});

busVolts.setValue(28.3);   // shows 28.3, right-aligned, leading zeros blanked
busVolts.setText(' E3');   // raw characters, one per cell
busVolts.setDashes();      // ---
busVolts.clear();          // blank
```

That one import is all you need. It also registers the extra digit styles listed under [Styles](#styles).

## Options

Only `digits` is required.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `digits` | required | Number of digit cells |
| `value` | `8` | Value shown at creation |
| `style` | `'classic'` | Digit style name, see [Styles](#styles) |
| `decimals` | `0` | Fixed number of decimal places |
| `digitHeight` | `100` | Height of each digit in px (the "font size") |
| `gap` | `8` | Space between cells in px |
| `color` | inherits CSS `color` | Color of lit segments |
| `offColor` | a faint default | Color of unlit segments |
| `offOpacity` | `0.10` | Opacity of unlit segments, 0 to 1 |
| `overflow` | `'dashes'` | What to show when the value needs more cells than exist: `'dashes'` or `'blank'` |
| `sign` | `false` | Reserve a fixed leading column for the minus sign |
| `ghost` | `'8.'` | Which unlit segments stay faintly visible: `'8.'` (all segments and the decimal point), `'8'`, `'1'`, `'0'`, or `''` (none) |
| `separators` | none | Cells to insert between digits, for example `[{ after: 1, type: 'colon' }]`. `after: -1` places one before the first digit |
| `position`, `left`, `top`, `right`, `bottom` | not set | CSS positioning of the whole readout |

## Styles

Digit styles, for the `style` option:

- Built in: `classic`, `block`, `slim`
- Added by this package: `sws_test1`, `sws_test2`, `sws_test_italic1`, `sws_d8_EIA`, `sws_d8_EIA2`, `sws_dash8`, `sws_dash8_italic`, `sws_dash8_bold_italic`, `sws_dash8_bold_italic_inner_border`

Separator types, for the `separators` option:

- `colon`, `dot`
- `sws_dash8_bold_italic_sign` and `sws_dash8_bold_italic_inner_border_sign`: a +/- sign cell that matches the digit style of the same name

A sign cell shows `+` when fully lit. Dim its vertical bar to show `-`:

```ts
const load = new SevenSegmentReadout(el, {
  digits: 3,
  decimals: 2,
  style: 'sws_dash8_bold_italic',
  separators: [{ after: -1, type: 'sws_dash8_bold_italic_sign' }],
});

load.setSeparatorOn(0, true);                     // show the sign cell
load.setSeparatorPartOn(0, 'seg-sign-v', false);  // vertical bar off: shows -
```

## Methods

Every option and method has a description that appears in your editor when you hover over it.

| Group | Methods |
|---|---|
| Value | `setValue`, `setText`, `setDashes`, `clear` |
| Whole readout | `setStyle`, `setDecimals`, `setDigitHeight`, `setGap`, `setColor`, `setOffColor`, `setGhost`, `setPosition` |
| One digit | `setDigitColor`, `setDigitScale`, `setDigitSize`, `setDigitPosition`, `setDigitVisible`, `setDigitGhost`, `setDigitOffColor`, `setDigitBlink`, `setDigitFlicker`, `setDigitClass` |
| One segment | `setSegmentColor`, `setSegmentClass`, `setSegmentFlicker` |
| Separators | `setSeparatorOn`, `setSeparatorPartOn`, `setSeparatorClass` |
| Extending | `registerStyle`, `registerGlyph` |

## Changing the library

1. Edit the files in `src/`.
2. Run `npm install` (first time only), then `npm run compile`.
3. Commit, including the `dist/` folder, and push.

```powershell
npm run compile
git add .
git commit -m "Describe the change"
git push
```

Things to know:

- **Always compile before committing.** Projects use the compiled files in `dist/`, not the ones in `src/`. Do not edit `dist/` by hand.
- **Adding a digit style:** add a `registerStyle(...)` call in `src/SevenSegmentLCDStyles.ts`. The markup must contain the classes `seg-a` to `seg-g` and `seg-dp`, and should not use `id` attributes.
- **Updating the guide:** edit `docs/guide/guide.html`, then run `node docs/guide/build-guide.mjs` to rebuild the PDF. It needs Chrome or Edge. The figures are drawn by the compiled library, so rebuild the guide after adding a style.
- **Script names:** do not add a script named `build`, `prepare`, `prepack`, `install`, `preinstall` or `postinstall` to `package.json`. npm would then run a full dependency install inside the package every time someone installs it.
